title: IngramSpark "Ink Coverage Exceeds 240%": What It Means & How to Fix | SparkPrep
description: IngramSpark rejected your file for ink coverage over 240%? Here's what total ink means, why rich black causes it, and how to fix it in Acrobat, InDesign or Word.
lead: This one sounds technical, but the cause is usually simple: black that's made from all four inks instead of black ink alone.
why:
Printers use four inks: cyan, magenta, yellow and black (CMYK). Total ink is all four added together in one spot. A pure black uses 100% (black only). A "rich black" can use 300% or more.

IngramSpark's limit is 240%. Over that, ink soaks the paper, smears and dries slowly, so the file is rejected. It often comes from black text in a file saved as RGB, or dark photos converted to CMYK without an ink limit.

steps: Tick Total Area Coverage and set it to 240%. Areas over the limit get highlighted.
Export it as grayscale (black ink only). Grayscale can never go over 100%, so the error disappears.
In Acrobat: Print Production → Convert Colors, convert everything to a grayscale profile.
Make black text 100% black (C0 M0 Y0 K100), not rich black.
Convert images to CMYK with a profile that limits total ink, such as US Web Coated (SWOP) v2 (300% max), then lower further if needed.
In InDesign, export with the PDF/X-1a preset and check Output Preview again.

cta.text: Don't want to learn color profiles to get one book printed? SparkPrep measures the ink on every page and brings it under 240% while keeping your black text sharp, in minutes.

faq.q: What is the IngramSpark ink limit?
faq.a: 240% total ink coverage, meaning cyan, magenta, yellow and black added together in any one area.

faq.q: How do I check total ink coverage?
faq.a: In Adobe Acrobat Pro, open Print Production, Output Preview and tick Total Area Coverage set to 240%. Anything over the limit is highlighted.

manual: Change all black text and black lines to 100% black only (C0 M0 Y0 K100), not "rich black".
For color pictures, convert them in Photoshop (Edit → Convert to Profile → Custom CMYK) with the total ink limit set to 240%.
Re-export as PDF/X-1a:2001, then check in Acrobat Pro (Print Production → Output Preview → Total Area Coverage at 240%) that nothing is highlighted.
Re-upload it to IngramSpark and wait for the file review and new e-proof.
